assessments.reasoning: The dated World Wide Web Consortium Recommendation, at the exact November 26, 2008 URL, identifies XML 1.0 Fifth Edition in its heading. Section 4.4.2 defines included replacement text as processed in the document in place of the reference. Pass-through is a processing obligation for covered character data. Inclusion and initial normalization determine which characters reach that processing path. The edition is the exact 2008 Recommendation and the statement limits delivery to processed document content, with entity data bound to inclusion. Section 4.4.3 allows a processor that is not validating to omit a covered external replacement text, with notification, and §5.1 defines the validation-specific inclusion obligations. limitations: Under §4.4.3, an XML processor that is not validating may omit replacement text for a recognized external parsed entity reference covered by that clause. If it omits the replacement text, it must notify the application that the entity was recognized and unread.

Under §5.1, validating processors read and process the entire DTD and referenced external parsed entities. The source separately specifies the obligatory processing of declarations read by non-validating processors.
Section 2.11 normalizes literal line endings before parsing. Section 2.10 also requires validating processors to identify white space in element content.
